Thirty-six changes since beta.6. The short version: backups no longer refuse your modded installations, installing a game version is lighter and safer, and notifications have a history you can go back to.

## Backups

Reported here and on the mod database: every automatic backup failed on installations of 4 GB and up. The launcher held backups to a 2 GB ceiling, a number borrowed from a check meant for archives downloaded from elsewhere, where a small file that unpacks into something enormous is a real attack. On your own game folder it never belonged. Backups now have their own limit of 64 GB, and the destination is checked for room before the archive starts.

A failed backup also used to stop the game with a generic error and nothing to do about it. It names the real cause now, disk full or permission denied, and asks whether to launch anyway for that one launch. Declining is the default, and the question comes back next time rather than quietly turning backups off for the installation.

## Installing a game version

Unpacking used to hold a whole compressed block in memory, over 1 GB on the reference installer. It streams now, under 200 MB. The install is staged and published by rename, so a crash halfway through no longer leaves a broken version folder, and on Windows a rename that fails part way no longer loses the files that were already there.

Leftovers from an interrupted run are cleaned on the next start. That cleanup only ever removes files the launcher itself wrote: an earlier form of it could have deleted an unrelated file of yours that happened to end in the same suffix.

## New

An Activity Center collects what the launcher has been doing, with a seen and read model, so a notification you missed while looking elsewhere is still there afterwards.

On Linux, an installation can carry a launch wrapper, so `gamemoderun`, `mangohud` or `prime-run` can front the game command per installation.

Manage Mods can filter installed mods by author, tag and supported game version, alongside the search added in beta.6.

## Fixed

A game version whose name the parser could not read is handled properly now: the launcher takes the version token out of the probe output instead of storing the whole line, so modded builds no longer land arbitrary text in the version field.

The mod catalog serves what it already has when you are offline instead of dropping a good list, and its disk cache is bounded. Mod logos fall back to the cached copy instead of disappearing. The Manage Mods spinner no longer runs forever when no installation is selected.

Background scenes refresh when they change, and the change now repaints the running session instead of waiting for a restart. Selecting a scene you already have no longer reports a download failure.

The updater shows progress before a cache-hit download instead of appearing to stall. Removing your last account now removes its recovery copies with it.

Grid and table rows expose their selected state and can be activated from the keyboard, and mod card actions are no longer nested inside the card's own button, which made them unreachable for keyboard and screen reader users.

## Under the hood

Startup is quicker: the updater loads when it is needed rather than on every launch, and the splash lifts when the window is ready. Every action button now comes from one system, so focus, disabled states and contrast behave the same everywhere. Renderer boundaries are hardened and pinned by tests. The packaged build dropped the unused Chromium locales, icons and dev scripts. Two dependency advisories were cleared, both in build-time packages that never ship inside the app.

The login dialog has labelled fields, states plainly that your credentials go to the Vintage Story auth service with a link to the privacy policy, and clears the password when it closes or a login is refused. A missing two-factor code no longer reports itself as an incorrect one.

The Linux documentation explains how community AUR packages and the built-in updater relate, after a question from the maintainer of `riftlauncher-bin`.

## Known issues

The Windows installer is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen and some antivirus tools warn on a fresh install. Every build here is produced by GitHub from the public source, and you can check any file on VirusTotal before running it. Signing is being sorted out.

macOS still has no build: the launcher cannot start the game there yet.
